notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 85-year-old male admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.59, creatinine 1.07-1.1, hemoglobin 12.8-14.3, platelets 212-219, sodium 140, wbc 6.8-7.2; vitals dbp 77-81, heart_rate 80-82, map 93-98, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 125-132, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. Acute blood loss anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.07-1.1, hemoglobin 11.7-12.5, platelets 208-215, sodium 140, wbc 6.9-7.5; vitals dbp 78-82, heart_rate 81-84, map 95-97, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 126-130, spo2 96-98, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 85-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Hypertension. No acute blood loss anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
